details: U.S. spot Bitcoin Exchange-Traded Funds (ETFs) are experiencing their worst month on record, with cumulative net outflows reaching approximately $5.39 billion in November. Despite these significant outflows, Bitcoin (BTC) rebounded above the $60,000 mark on Thursday, tracking a rise in broader risk assets during holiday trading. Analysts note that persistent ETF outflows weaken spot demand, increasing downside risks and limiting sustainable rallies.
title: Bitcoin ETFs See Record Outflows as Price Recovers Above $60K

details: Ethereum (ETH) has crossed the $1,700 benchmark, showing a 3.08% increase in 24 hours. This price movement occurred while a long-dormant Ethereum wallet from the network's 2014 presale offloaded approximately 32,010 ETH, valued at about $53.3 million, to major exchanges Binance and Bybit. U.S. spot Ether ETFs have also seen significant net outflows of around $1.23 billion in November, reflecting caution among institutional investors.
sourceName: Binance News / BigGo Finance (citing CoinGecko, BeInCrypto)
title: Ethereum Surpasses $1,700 Amidst Dormant Wallet Activity

details: Auros, a Hong Kong-based crypto trading and market-making firm, is reportedly winding down its operations. The company's co-founder previously stated in July 2024 that Auros handled roughly 4% of global crypto exchange trading volume. The reasons and timetable for the wind-down are not yet clear.
title: Crypto Market Maker Auros Reportedly Winding Down Operations

details: Galaxy Research has retracted its earlier call that Bitcoin's bear market concluded in June. The firm indicated that the signal supporting its previous assessment has failed and warned that a daily close below Bitcoin's June 30 low of $58,525 could initiate a move to a "materially lower low."
title: Galaxy Research Withdraws Bitcoin Bear Market End Call

details: The UK's financial regulator is reportedly planning to introduce stricter rules for decentralized finance (DeFi), citing the recent $6.3 billion Binance hack as a key concern. This move indicates a harder line on DeFi regulation in the UK compared to approaches taken in the US and EU.
title: UK Regulator Plans Tougher DeFi Rules Following Binance Hack

details: Spain's financial intelligence unit, Sepblac, will soon have the authority to temporarily freeze cryptocurrency accounts for up to five working days without prior court authorization. This new provision, part of a consumer lending decree, is aimed at combating money laundering and terrorist financing and is set to take effect on January 25, 2027, pending parliamentary approval.
title: Spain to Allow Temporary Crypto Account Freezes Without Court Approval
